    <h4 style="font-weight: bold; margin-top: -5px;">Pilgrim Society—Remembering Plymouth</h4>
    <br />
    <p>Of old New England stock, Associate Justice David H. Souter could trace his ancestors back to the landing of the Mayflower in 1620. Souter was born in Massachusetts in 1939, graduated from both Harvard and Harvard Law School, and practiced law in Concord, New Hampshire, before starting a long record of public service. Five years after joining the Supreme Court in 1990, Justice Souter was invited to participate in the 375th anniversary ceremony of the Pilgrims’ landing at Plymouth Rock, Massachusetts. The event included a naturalization ceremony for 104 new citizens during which Justice Souter administered the oath and spoke briefly about the connection between the Mayflower Compact and the U.S. Constitution. In recognition of his participation in the event, the Pilgrim Society gifted Justice Souter with a membership certificate and plaque commemorating his contribution to “Citizenship Day, July 23, 1995.”</p>
